And, at the same time, I do understand from your earlier portion of the cross-examination that that was exactly what everyone was entitled to, is to group themselves together and to defend the constitutional structure of the Federal Republic of the Socialist Yugoslavia - SFRY, I should say - Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Now I'm just trying to understand what you're telling us. Are you telling it was everyone's right? And then I have difficulties on why you insist so much on the MUP not starting in 1993 but already in 1991, against what then apparently was everyone's right. Is -- is -- I'm trying to -- or is it that you say, No, it was wrong, the MUP took action against it. And then I have difficulties in understanding this legislation which suggests that it was everyone's right to do that. So I'm -- the only thing I'm doing at this moment is trying to understand the message you're sending to us through the cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is what my message is: This case deals with Croatia and Bosnia territorially. It deals with a period when what was in force in that area was the Law on Defence of the SFRY and when the Serbs, in those areas, could organise themselves and prepare for defence and self-defence. I think that that is something that we are going to find useful in the further proceedings ahead of us. That is one point. My other point is that I've tried to show that various volunteer groups could not just stroll about with weapons. However, what the law did allow was that in a state of war and an imminent threat of war the army and the MUP could organise legal centres, in which, perhaps, the training of volunteers could take place but within a legal framework. What we showed now and what Mr. Theunens tried to say, and I believe that's part of his report too, is that the MUP of Serbia tolerated various armed groups that had come from Croatia [as interpreted] and then they committed crimes there and milled about Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, the only thing I was not seeking, Mr. Bakrac, of course, doesn't give evidence, but since I was a bit confused about what I was supposed to understand from this evidence that I asked him, that's perhaps not very common. But, at the same time, you'll understand that the Chamber, if it feels that it might lose track, that it tries to get itself on track again, whether or not we agree in every respect with what Mr. Bakrac said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I understand that that's what the Trial Chamber was doing. I just wanted to correct the representation of Mr. Theunens's evidence on page 66, line 13. I believe Mr. Theunens did testify during cross-examination last week that the groups originated from Serbia, not Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac. Arms group comes from Croatia and they committed crimes there, milled about Serbia. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it must have been my mistake. I wanted to say that they were coming back from Croatia. So I did not word it properly. They were returning from Croatia and Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's clear to me. We will have a break and resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, did you have an opportunity to look at what we've discussed over the break?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you refer to what I've asked to you look at over the break so as not to repeat everything I've said.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. First question was to provide examples of the security administration of the SFRY armed forces informing the MUP of Serbia. There is one document, P1060, at page 93 of part 1 of my report. The other documents - and I refer specifically to information reports by security organs of the 1st Military District, which are sent to the SSNO -- excuse me, to the security administration at the SSNO - do not allow to conclude what the security administration at the SSNO did with these documents, and, I mean, these documents can be found in part 2, pages 88 to 96. And if I remember well, you also asked me about documents indicating knowledge of the MUP Serbia of --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, my apologies for interrupting you, but I just would like to follow up on something you said. From what I understand, you found only one document which indicates that the security administration informed the MUP of some events. If my understanding is correct, the other documents went to the SSNO security administration, but there is no further evidence indicating that they reached MUP. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. And just to clarify, there would be no reason for these documents of the first -- excuse me, of the security organ of the 1st Military District to be sent directly to the MUP. The normal chain would be security organs of the 1st Military District to the security administration at the SSNO, and then the security administration at the SSNO would be in charge of informing the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: However, we have no evidence whatsoever that this was indeed what the SSNO administration did, i.e., inform the MUP about all these events; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have only been able to identify one document. Of course, we can assume that there are more documents but I understand your question in that regard. There's only one document I could identify that was available to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, let us focus on this sole document. Save for conveying information, did you see any sort of evidence being attached to the document or any other supporting documentation corroborating the fact that the MUP -- or, rather, supplementing the information in order to enable the MUP to react, or is it merely a report on some events?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, we discussed P1060 during cross-examination by Mr. Jordash, and it shows a number of comments the Ministry of Interior provides to the document; for example, reminding the military security administration of the military justice procedure in relation to alleged perpetrators who belonged to the military. And there's also information on other people. I mean, we would have to look at the document again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. This is my next question, Mr. Theunens: Did the security administration fulfil its duty by simply informing the MUP? Did the security administration through its own organs, i.e., military police, and through the security organs, take measures in its area of responsibility in respect of the crimes that it was allegedly given notice of?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the absence of specific documents, I cannot draw a conclusion -- or I cannot provide an answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. And now for the second part. I interrupted you giving me the answer.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honours, I understand that the question was to identify documents that show that the MUP of Republic of Serbia had knowledge of or provided support to Arkan. When I say "had knowledge of," it means activities, including illegal activities, conducted by Arkan, or Zeljko Raznjatovic. This is covered in part 1, pages 101 to 108. And for what alleged crimes is concerned, in part 2, pages 78 to 96. If you want, can I read out the P numbers, but ... yeah -- I can also refer you to the sections in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, my question was: What was the evidence indicating that volunteer units were being prevented from going through training or -- or milling about in uniform and with weapons, what was the evidence indicating that they were prevented from doing so only from 1993 onwards?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... perhaps I give you the details of the source. Part of your evidence was that you said that somebody like Seselj, for example, relied on the - call it tacit - authorisation of the Serbian authorities. And his relationship with Slobodan Milosevic is good relation with Slobodan Milosevic, in order to organise and so on -- the -- his groups, and that only when there was a political fallout between November -- between the two in November 1993, that legal steps were put against this volunteers. That was, I think, one part of your -- the second being that you said -- was about your testimony, I think, in the Seselj case, where it was put to you that you said: "This is not dealt with in my report, but I remember that it's only after a political conflict arises between Mr. Seselj and Mr. Milosevic, sometime in October -- November 1993, that the competent authorities in Serbia start with the arrest of volunteers. And they are all arrested, or most of them are arrested, on the grounds of illegal possession of fire-arms and they're released quite soon." Mr. Bakrac -- that was the evidence you gave, and Mr. Bakrac is looking for the sources that it was only in or after November 1993 that such action was taken and not any earlier. Mr. Bakrac, that was your question. And I've given you now, literally, the portions of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I apologise, but I was confused by the reference to -- by Mr. Bakrac to Serbian Volunteer Guard, and I thought -- when he was formulating his question. As I mentioned earlier today, I have not -- I don't think I have included any document in my report -- this report here, showing that SRS volunteers were arrested in the course of -- or after November 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, the question was on what documentary basis -- it's clear that you indicated on from November 1993 that arrests took place, as you described.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But on what basis you concluded that a similar thing did not happen before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honours. Well, when you look at parts 2 and part 3 of the report, you see that SRS SCP volunteers participate in a number of -- in the -- sorry, in the conflict in a number of areas of Croatia in 1991. I have discussed Sector West and -- excuse me, Western Slavonia; Western Slavonia and Slavonia, Baranja, Western Srem. And we then noticed that sometimes the same SRS volunteers or other SRS volunteers also participate in a number of takeover operations in northern Bosnia-Herzegovina that are conducted in spring 1992. I conclude from that that the Serbian authorities, including the Ministry of Interior of Republic of Serbia, allowed these groups to conduct these kind of activities. The reference to November 1993 then is based on the fact that only documents I have seen here at the OTP that mention arrests of SRS volunteers date from November 1993 or afterwards. There are a number of documents, but, again, I haven't discussed that here, but there is -- attempts are made, I believe, in the course of 1994 to put a number -- I think two members of the Yellow Wasps on trial in Serbia, but that trial is repeatedly delayed, and I don't recall from the top of my head if there's ever an outcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, that Mr. Bakrac did put this question to you in the following context, without elaborating on it. He referred to the -- to testimony which indicated that persons could not bring arms with them in a bus when going to a training centre because they feared that the MUP would intervene, which, as I understand Mr. Bakrac well, suggests that the MUP already, at that time, in 1991, did not leave such groups, or whatever you want to call them, didn't leave them -- well, acted against them, or at least that they thought that action might be taken against them if they would travel with weapons in their possession.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honours, and I will basically repeat what I said earlier. That, indeed - and, again, this is based on documents I reviewed - that initially -- and there is a document, P1051, from 25th of July, 1991; it's a public statement of the minister of defence of the Republic of Serbia. There's also -- there are statements of SRS volunteers indicating that initially the Serbian authorities are opposed to the establishment of these groups; I mean, party-affiliated volunteer groups. However, over time, and I would say at the latest by fall 1991, these groups are authorised to exist, to organise themselves, to train. And we discussed the existence of the training centre in Prigrevica, whereby Prigrevica - I looked on the map during the break - is located in Vojvodina. The documents I have seen -- I mean, several documents indicate that there was indeed a training centre which was used by the SRS. I have not seen a document that indicates that the Serbian MUP prevented that training centre from operating, at least not in 1991. And I don't remember for 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So let me try to understand, then, to perhaps summarize your answer. You say, in the very beginning there was some opposition or action taken against them, then there was a period in which they were left alone more or less and were condoned in their activities, and then after a clash between Mr. Seselj and Mr. Milosevic in November 1993 they started arresting, but after that, again, from what I understand, they were further condoned and there was an understanding of the usefulness of the existence of them. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. And, I mean, this applies to the SRS volunteers. And we also have to note that after -- I mean, in November 1993 there is very limited indication that SRS volunteers are still active in Croatia because conflict is finished. I mean, there is also a cease-fire or a cessation of hostilities in end of 1991. We know that in January 1993 efforts are undertaken by the SRS to send volunteers to Sector South because the Croatian armed forces have conducted an attack in the pink zone in Maslenica. But during -- at that time there are only SRS volunteers in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and there is much less information on any -- for example, travel of these people or armed travel of these people to Serbia, or the training of additional SRS volunteers in the Republic of Serbia at that time. So the requirement for action of the minister of interior of the Republic of Serbia seems to lessor, except, of course, if it comes to the investigation of alleged crimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, you received answers to your questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. With your leave, I'd try to have a couple of points clarified further.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that you thought that the MUP of Serbia condoned these groups in their organising as military groups and getting training at various training centres. Based on what evidence do you claim that the MUP was aware of, say, the volunteer training centre in Vojvodina, which was an abandoned farming estate, which would lead you to draw the conclusion that the MUP of Serbia tacitly approved of such a training centre?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The prolonged existence of the training centre shows that no action was undertaken to close it. I haven't seen a document that shows that it was closed upon an action of the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia. And since this training centre is used to train non-government-controlled armed groups, it would be a violation of Article 118 of the Law on Defence, but that's just one aspect --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just stop you here. The first question of Mr. Bakrac is awareness. I mean, if something exists for a long time, of course, it's not closed. But the first question was whether there was any awareness. Because if there's no awareness, it might be difficult to close something. That would be the first part of the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honours. I have not seen -- I mean, I don't remember seeing a document that the MUP of Serbia was aware of the existence of the Prigrevica training centre at the time it existed. There is a lot of -- there are a lot of SRS publications on the training centre, but I would have to check from which time-period they date. Now, on the other hand, I would assume that it's -- since the MUP is tasked to ensure, among others, law and order and -- and preserve state security, that they wouldn't just wait till they are -- till they explicitly received the information but would also actively gather information on -- not just on such groups, but also the activities and the training centre, the centres they may use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was part of the question. At the farm at a far distance the suggestion was clearly by Mr. Bakrac that it might have remained unnoticed due to the location of the training centre. Is that something which sounds reasonable to you? Is there anything you would like to comment on? Because you say they would not wait for information. But if it's far away and if they don't -- if in the normal acquiring of information you might miss that information, then, of course, it doesn't come as a surprise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot provide a direct answer because I haven't seen the facility; but among the documents I have received from the Defence, there are reports that, for example, organs of the state security are monitoring Arkans bakery in Belgrade. And, of course, that's a very visible building, and somebody -- if -- I would think that -- and, again, it's maybe speculation, but looking at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's refrain from speculation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let's finish this off. You said the long existence of the centre, do you have any specific data? I mean, the starting and the closing date of the centre?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the specific dates, but I've seen documents referring to -- I mean, dated 1991 and 1992 that indicate the existence of the training centre during those time-periods. But I cannot give a precise opening nor closing date. But if you want, I can --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you want, I can --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have an electronic version of my Seselj report, if that can assist the Trial Chamber. And I can do -- conduct searchs there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps if you -- perhaps do that this evening.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you're able to do it without too many efforts. So if we can get an answer to that question, it would be appreciated. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, there's an another issue you mentioned that I'd like to clarify with you. You said that the volunteers fought in Slavonia and Bosnia. Did the Serbian MUP have powers to arrest them in these areas?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand you're asking about the SRS volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. That's what you were discussing.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. No, but as I mentioned earlier during my testimony, these volunteers were transiting through Serbia and some were even living in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know, and can you tell us with certainty, that these volunteers passed across Serbia under full combat gear and with weapons on their way to Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina, or are you not able to tell us that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember specific documents. I mean, another facility, for example, was the -- the camp in Bubanj Potok which is in Belgrade. It used to be --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We will -- I apologise. I put a very specific question to you. We will come back to the Bubanj Potok camp later on, and we will be discussing legal and illegal camps and we will see who that camp was run by. The question was specific: Do you have a single piece of evidence that volunteers - and we are discussing the Serbian Radical Party volunteers at the moment - on their way to Bosnia-Herzegovina and Croatia transited through Serbia or travelled through Serbia with weapons as a group?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, this is again -- I mean, it's a pity that I don't have my Seselj report here, but there is an aspect that I have covered in that report in an sense that I remember that certain volunteers received weapons permits, to travel with weapons. But I would have to check whether this was in the Republic of Serbia or by the local Serb authorities in Croatia or Bosnia-Herzegovina. And I also have a recollection that -- that in Bubanj Potok there were -- I mean, volunteers received weapons. Now, I cannot confirm how these -- whether they then subsequently travelled with their weapons. But I will check my Seselj report for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. Let's move on. I asked you about the area of responsibility, which is an issue that is related to what we just discussed. Let's look at P1390, which is a document you gave your comments on during the examination by my learned friend Mr. Weber. Specifically page 2 in both versions. There's item 5.K, which I suppose is the 5th Corps. So it's the area of the 2nd Military District, and it's the 10th of April, 1992, operational combat report. Do you recall discussing this document with the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe we discussed this document when we were looking at the situation in Zvornik at the time. Yeah, I have a reference to it on page 60 of part 3 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, look at the first line under 5th corps. The focus of the work of the corps command was on the firm grip of the front lines, control over the territory both along the length of the front line and in the depth. The situation in the area of the corps is becoming increasingly complex and it's especially difficult in the area of Jajce and is getting ever more serious in the area of Prijedor and Sanski Most. So can we conclude on the basis of this that the 5th Corps of the Army of Yugoslav, i.e., the 2nd Military District, controlled both the length of the front line and its depth. In other words, the entire area of responsibility that it had. And does it follow from this document that it was its duty to do so?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. But okay the document does not indicate the -- the zone of responsibility, but it states, as you state, as you mentioned, they're holing the front line, and there's also -- they're also conducting territory control in the rear.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So if it says "control over the territory and the rear," they had the responsibility for the situation in that particular territory; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would have to see at the -- again, the situation there. Are there still functioning or are there functioning civilian authorities, and what has been established in relation to the the links or the relations between these civilian authorities and the 5th Corps?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So we're talking about the 10th of April, 1992, aren't we? Now look at the 9th Corps. The corps units were engaged in holding the front line and carrying out operations in the area of Kupres, taking in soldiers from the 3rd Military District, and manning the JTO, the Territorial Defence unit, and the units of the Serb Krajina. So will you agree with me that the 9th Corps, here, has the powers to man the Territorial Defence unit and the units of the police, the milicija, of the Republic of the Serb Krajina?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, these powers - if you can -- if one would use the word powers there - these are part of the mission the 9th Corps has received from the SFRY -- SFRY armed forces Supreme Command, i.e., a political body.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, sorry --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I need to correct. The Supreme -- I mean, the SFRY forces' Supreme Command issues political instructions to the Supreme Command Staff, and the Supreme Command Staff translates these political instructions into military orders which are then passed downwards through the chain of command, which would be, in this case, from the Supreme Command Staff, to the 2nd Military District, to the 9th Corps. And I'm sorry for the confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Theunens, could you now have a look at the 17th Corps. That was the corps that was responsible for Bosanski Samac; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It says here the corps units are at full combat readiness and they're engaged in preparing mobilised units, securing the traffic on the main roads, and monitoring the situation at crisis points in the area of responsibility. So this 17th Corps, on the 10th of April - and later on we're going to get to the topic of Bosanski Samac as well - is reporting that they are basically engaged on preparing the mobilised units, securing conditions for traffic on the main roads, and monitoring the situation at crisis points in the area of their responsibility. Do you agree that that was -- that was a comprehensive monitoring of the situation, the responsibility of the 17th Corps for the situation in the area, even taking care of traffic and roads so that passengers and volunteers could move about, and so on?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really understand your question. Because are you suggesting that the 17th Corps is the only organisation that is able to conduct these missions, or what -- I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I accept that perhaps I am somewhat confused and that I did not put the question properly. I'll try to rephase. So look at the end of the sentence: Monitoring the situation at crisis points in the zone of responsibility. And before that we see all the things that the 17th Corps is doing. Do you agree with me that the 17th Corps was responsible for the situation in the zone of its responsibility? That includes Bosanski Samac as well.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, the question could be asked which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, what exactly are you asking? Are you asking on the basis of this document? This document describes what activities were deployed by -- in this case, the 17th Corps. Well, are you relying on Mr. Theunens's knowledge from other sources, or are you relying on his interpretation of this document? For example, if you say "securing the traffic on the main roads," it could mean everything. You translate that into civilians being -- what could also be civilians not to be allowed on the roads. I mean, it could be anything. At least on the basis of the text we see here, you are giving your own interpretation. Now, fine, no problem. If Mr. Theunens shares that interpretation, then he will tell us. But what I'm interested to know whether you're just interpreting a text or whether you're asking Mr. Theunens, while interpreting this text, to rely on other information he may have. That's my concern about your question at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I did understand. And I'm going to try to do away with any possible dilemmas. I had ask Mr. Theunens earlier on what an area of responsibility is from the point of view of military doctrine. Now I'm asking him the following. We know that a state of imminent threat of war was declared in 1991; that's the document dated the 10th of April, 1992. So now I'm asking whether the 17th Corps had authority and whether they had the responsibility and duty to control the territory in its zone and to arrest possible perpetrators of crimes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document does not allow to draw any conclusions on that, because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's, first. Mr. Bakrac, are you asking Mr. Theunens to rely on this document to draw conclusions from that, or are you asking him to combine what is found in this report with other evidence he has?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I would like Mr. Theunens to tell me from a doctrinary point of view to answer my question, the one that I had already put: namely, in this situation - and we see from this report what it is the 17th Corps is doing - whether the 17th Corps has the right and responsibility within its area of responsibility, according to the rules of the military profession, to exercise control over the territory and arrest perpetrators of crimes or investigate crimes that are committed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean, I will try my best. But the wording is so general, because what kind of crimes? What kind of perpetrators? Is it the traffic violation, is it a war crime?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I'll try to be more specific. If, in the month of April 1992, some person that was subordinated to the command of the 17th Corps had committed a war crime or murder, for example in Sakvina [phoen] for instance. The security organ, the military police, are they responsible to investigate it, arrest the perpetrators, and conduct criminal proceedings against them? Also, if they are subordinated to that command.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a totally different question, because, as we discussed over the previous days, in any event, I mean, and this applies to all members of -- all officers of the JNA, and I refer again to Article 36 of the 1988 regulations on the implementation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, sorry to interrupt you. Let's try to see whether we can deal with it in a rather quick way. 17th Corps in the place where it is deployed, if a soldier subordinated to that corps command commits a war crime, would it fall within the scope of the competence of the military police to investigate, arrest, et cetera, that person? Let me first see. Mr. Weber, would you ... is that a contested issue at all? Not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have two parties agreeing and an expert agreeing on the matter. Let's move on with the next question. Because in your earlier questions, Mr. Bakrac - and that was confusing Mr. Theunens - you did not specify at all. And it was only in the last version of your question that you talked about someone who was subordinated and you talked about a war crime. So that seems to be not in dispute. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could we now have in e-court 65 ter number 2793, Prosecution number. So we're going to go back to something that we have already discussed in part, Mr. Theunens. This is another Prosecution document, and I would be interested in the following: When writing up your report, did you have an opportunity of seeing it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have seen the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this is one example. And there's another one too. And then we are going to complete a subject that we had already raised. We see here that there is a stamp as well: "Association of veterans from the municipality of Arandjelovac." And obviously they are registered as a citizens' association because they have a stamp of their own. And they are confirming that Captain Zoran Baltic from Arandjelovac and Captain Dimce Mijantovic of Zenjanin [phoen] are volunteers, members of the Army of Republika Srpska, Military Post 7202, Red Berets special purpose unit. And that the above-mentioned persons are travelling on business for the purpose of visiting the wounded and collecting humanitarian aid for Republika Srpska. So -- actually, first of all, these are members of the Army of Republika Srpska, the Red Berets that originally come from the territory of Serbia. They are under a military post outside Serbia. And they are travelling in order to collect humanitarian aid. Does the MUP of Serbia have any reason to arrest such persons?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends what they do in the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or if the MUP has received any information from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's all speculation. Do you want the witness to answer this question on the basis of this document? Because then the question is very simple: Whether persons serving as volunteers which are qualified as members of the Army of the Republika Srpska Red Berets special purpose units, that if they're travelling in order to visit the wounded and to collect humanitarian aid for the Republika Srpska, whether there's any reason in that to arrest them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the face of this document, there is no reason to arrest them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you want to ask the same question in relation to other knowledge Mr. Theunens may have or may not have? Do you have any knowledge which would shed further light on this specific situation, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then -- was this, by the way, any matter in dispute? Mr. Weber, I'm looking at you. The question as I phrased it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is some facts in there that would be partially disputed. I just would note. And I don't want to offer too much information in front of this witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I'm not asking whether you dispute the facts. I'm was asking whether the question, as based on this document, assuming - not establishing, assuming - that this is the whole of the story, whether there would be any reason to arrest the man?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could we now have, in relation to this, 65 ter number 4830. It's a Prosecution number.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this is an Official Note. It's from the Prosecution collection. Please have a look at it and tell me whether you've seen it before, when you were preparing to write your report and to testify here.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, there's a name in the document that looks familiar, but I don't remember whether I saw the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, the centre of the State Security Service in Subotica, the third section, in August 1993, that is to say, even before that month of November that you had referred to, is following extremism. And an employee of the State Security Service, a certain S. Jankovic - and you're going to see that in the paragraph that starts with the following words: "Through the 1990 war veterans association" - it's a document similar to the one that we have seen - "the members of this paramilitary formation are sent to the front line in the Republic of the Serb Krajina under the command of Lieutenant Slobodan Ristic, a former waiter at the JNA centre in Subotica. Before leaving for the front as an agent of the Yugoslav Army security organ, through the Subotica garrison chief of military security, Koca Milenkovic, Ristic managed to obtain weapons and equipment for around ten members of the SRS, transfer the weapons and ammunition to Belgrade, and store it in the Jugobanka cellar and vault." So is it correct that the State Security Service is monitoring the situation and providing information to the effect that under the auspices of the security organs of the Army of Yugoslavia such things are being done?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what the document states.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: On the other hand, we saw that the security administration is purportedly giving some useful information to the MUP and is shifting responsibility for things that had been committed to the MUP; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, this document, or any other source of knowledge? Because the document says that the information is passed on; and, as far as I've seen, nothing has been said on who now has the responsible to do what. Could you please clearly phrase your question, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I withdraw the question. What Mr. Theunens has already told me is sufficient. I do apologise. I am truly going into an area of speculation. And in order to avoid that, I withdraw the question, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my previous answer, I just confirmed what the document states.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we can -- if we're talking about the document, the document reports on what apparently -- what kind of activity was developed and -- yes, it's -- it says what it says. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We had been dealing with Arkan before the break. We'll go back to that. Could I now have P367, please. Lest there be any confusion, because the document that I have already shown speaks of cooperation. So can I have P367. It has two pages. Could the witness please have a look at the first page and then the second page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the document should not be shown to the public, being under seal. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour, I wasn't paying attention. P367, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I do not fully remember why it was under seal. Could you please keep that in mind when -- in order to consider requesting going into private session. Again, I do not know. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It was in relation to a 92 quater matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 92 quater matter. May I take it that there's no -- is there any need, in view of the content of the document, to ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No, it's fine. It's fine to be shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's fine. Okay. Please proceed. You can ask the questions in open session, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, could you please be so kind as to look at this diagram. All the participants on the first page and on the second page, this document speaks of joint operations. And then you will tell me whether we can conclude, on the basis of this document, that Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, was under the command of the 51st Mechanized Brigade in this operation, or, rather, under the command of Enes Taso, 51st Mechanised Brigade. Once you've had a look at it, could you please give us a sign so that we can display page 2 for you as well?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen page 1 and it doesn't mention Arkan, because it shows the peacetime structure of the 51st Mechanized Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Precisely, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could I now please have page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: That's exactly what I wanted to clarify, whether they were subordinated ...

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon, the third page. I do apologise. My mistake. I'm sorry, I am tired.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I should maybe ask about the source of the document, but I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- again, let's -- Mr. Bakrac, what do you want Mr. Theunens to tell us? To interpret this document on the basis of what the document says, or do you want him to interpret that document on the basis of not only the content of this document but also on other knowledge he may or may not have?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my original idea was, basically, not to show this document, because Mr. Theunens himself had said that they had been subordinated in combat operations. However, because of that other document, there was this lack of clarity. My response to your question is that I would like Mr. Theunens, if possible, both on the basis of this document and on the basis of the other document, to confirm whether Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, was under the command of the Army of Yugoslavia in combat operations. The JNA, sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know -- Your Honours, I know the source of this document, but maybe we should go in closed session because I just want to make sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into -- private session will do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Private, I'm ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The transcript is bit unclear as to when the Chamber expects the reply to the response to the 18th motion to amend the 65 ter list. Where the transcript may say 15th of November, I think I said the 5th of November. That is, this Friday. I hope that that's clear and was clear already. Then the second issue, we've heard that both Defence teams do not oppose against Prosecution replying to the Defence response to the first bar table motion, and we'd like to receive your reply by the 10th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, if there's nothing else, we adjourn for the day. And we resume tomorrow, the 2nd of November, 2010, at 9.00 in the morning, in Courtroom II.
